- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.68) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.35) and prices are rising, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to capture momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (≥5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; apply a 2–5% downward correction in subsequent periods.
- If model forecast is consistently below true outcome over 3–5 periods, suggest mean reversion bias — adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% per period until convergence.
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.3–0.7), model often fails to capture short-term reversals; use sentiment-weighted smoothing (e.g., 70% recent, 30% prior) to dampen noise.
- If true outcome exceeds model by >2% for 2+ consecutive periods, assume “sentiment-driven breakout”; increase forecast by 1–2% for next period to align with momentum.
